GENERAL REQUIREMENTS FOR TENTS (First Revision )

FOREWORD
General of Supplies been included; b) and Disposals have

0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 10 February 1988, after the draft finalized by the Made Up Textiles (other than ReadyMade Garments ) Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile -Division Council. 0.2 This standard originally published in 1975, was abased on G/Tex/T-IG `General specification for tent components and fabrication' issued by and the Directorate General of Supplies ~;J;~g;ls Ed IND/TC/2245( ,c ) `General speci. tents ( textrle ) , issued by the Ministry of Defence, Government of India. The revision has been undertaken to present incorporate the following major changes: a) Details of packing of various of tents as followed by the components Directorate

Cotton line of only 4fimm dia has been prescribed instead of 1~3 mm and 16 mm circumference cotton lines specified in different components of the tent earlier;

strength test of jute canvas c) For breaking used in the manufacture of S`4LITHAS and bags, ravelled strip test method has been prescribed. Further, for testing of other requirements of jute canvas, method of tests as prescribed in IS : 10036 ( Part l)1982* have been referred to; and d) References to all latest Indian have been made in this revised Staudards version.

_ *Specification for jute canvas: Part 1 General requiremenu.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard specifies the requirements of materials, components, manufacturing, workmanship and packing of tents.
2. MATERIALS

2.1 The

materials used in the fabrication tents and other related items shall conform the requirements given in Table 1. 3. MANUFACTURE

shall be fitted in the form of a loop to the inside portion of the detachable wall to prevent excessive flapping of the wall in high ~wind. It shall be constructed of 2 nor 3 folds of duck or canvas as in 3.1.1 and covered on both sides with one fold of dasuti of shade matching with the background. 3.1.3 The ropes shall fit the holes of the tabs tightly. The holes in the corner and side tabs shall be punched out first to a size slightly less than that of the rope to be used. The holes shall be carefully stitched as in case of button holes with 12 to 14 stitches per hole with 2 mm diameter cotton line or two strands of cotton sewing thread of 590 dtex x 3 ( lost3 ) count; the length of stitch shall not be more than 13 mm. 3.2 Plies 3.2.1 Each fold of cloth shall be made of complete length except where construction makes this impossible. Short length pieces measuring not less than one metre may be used provided the cross-seams are made at the joints and these -pieces are staggered in such a way that they do not appear side by side in the same panel or face each other in the adjoining panels. 3.2.2 All strengthening tapes length throughout without any edges securely sewn to the-folds the ends secured well within the 1 shall be of one joint and both of cloth and all tabs and caps.

3.1 Caps, Tabs and Guide Loops 3.1.1 Caps and Tabs -- Caps and tabs shall be made of duck or canvas with 3 folds in case the mass is 500 g/m2 or less and 2 folds if it exceeds 500 g/m'. Each half portion shall be machinesewn on the edge with cotton sewing thread of 165 dtex x 6 (36 s/6) count for ultimate fitting to the fly. Two caps or tabs shall then be placed on either side of the fly to which they are to be attached and securely sewn by machine in double rows using cotton sewing thread of 590 dtex X 3 ( lOs/3 ) count having 16 to 20 stitches/ dm or with MOCHI stitches with 2 mm dia cotton line. The length of the MOCHI stitches shall not be more than 25 mm. These shall be well covered on the exposed side with fabric of the same shade as that of the part of the fly to which they are attached.

NOTE 1 -Each fold of cloth shall be made up in complete lengths except where narrow widths or croasseams are allowed. Narrow width panels shall be allowed subject to maximum of one in each fold of all the walls provided these panels are staggered and no panel is less than 10 cm in width. A maximum of four narrow width panels shall be permitted in all outer and inner flies ( two in the outer and two in the inner fly ) provided However, the corner panel of single pole square these panels are staggered and are not less than 20 cm in width. The finished width of the narrow panr,lr when tents and similar flies may have a minimum width of 10 cm. measured at caves shall be not less than 25 and 21.5 cm respectively, in respect of 80 and 50 kg tents. 3.3.2 In the case of inner fly, the ridge shall be formed ~by inserting a strip of 100 mm wide NEWAR ( unless otherwise specified in the particular specification ) between the fold alongwith an 8 mm dia cotton rope. The cotton rope shall be so laid on the underside of the ridge and over the middle tape situated between the caps that the cloth of the fly and centre strip of NEWAR shall be doubled over the rope, and sewn together with 2 mm diameter cotton line to form a beading. Loops made of 50 mm wide JVEWAR or a cloth bag made of two folds of cloth ( unless otherwise specified in the particular specification ) shall be stitched to the ridge of the inner fly for suspending it from the ridge pole. 3.3.3 In a single fly tent, the ridge shall be formed by a strip of 75 mm wide .NEWAR and 8 mm dia rope piping ( unless otherwise specified in the particular specification ). KANATS

3.4.1 The KARATS shall be made in such a way that they are capable of being fixed upright and secured firmly in position and yet be easily detachable.
3.4.2 Aluminium eyelets shall be fixed at the top edge of the KAJVAT at intervals of about 23 cm to correspond with the loop made from 4 mm dia cotton line, fixed in the centre of JVEWAR at the bottom edge of the inner fly. The KAJVAT shall be provided with bamboo uprights as stays ( if so specified in the respective specification ) inserted between the folds of cloth and shall be enclosed in two strips of 65 mm wide .NEWAR running between the bamboo and the inside fold. The ends of bamboo shall be covered with tabs. The number of bamboo uprights in the KARAT shall correspond with the XEWAR placed in the inner fly to which it shall be joined. A strip of 65 mm wide NE WAR shall be provided eat the top edge and 10 mm dia rope enclosed in 65 mm wide NEb4'AR at the bottom edge of the KAJVAT. NEWARS shall be securely quilted to the cloth. 3.4.3 A 23 cm loop made with 8 mm dia cotton rope shall be attached to the bottom of each upright by means of the tab. 3.4.4 A frill of NE WAR shall be sewn all round at the bottom edge of the KA.NAT if specified in the respective specification. 3.5 Flaps (

3.5.3 For tents of2'44 x 2'44 m size and over, each flap shall be provided with two vertical strengthening .NE WARS placed between the folds of fabrics as is done in the case of flies (see 3.2.3). One of these NEWARS shall be placed along the inside edge of the flap at the centre of the tent width and the other midway between this inside edge JVEWAR and the off side edge of the flap. Unless otherwise specified in the particular specification, 6 aluminium eyelets shall be fixed olr'the inside flap. In case of tents of smaller size, a vertical strengthening .NEWAR shall be placed between the folds of fabrics along the inside edge of each flap at the centre of the tent width. Unless otherwise specified in the particular specification, 5 aluminium eyelets shall be fixed on the inside flap. 3.5.4 Two pieces of cotton tape NEWAR of 25 mm width and 60 cm length shall be sewn along the juction of the fly and flap-one 30 cm inside and the other 30 cm outside, for tying the flaps when rolled up. 3.5.5 NEWARS shall be securely quilted to the cloth folds. Metal dees or foot loops (as specified in the respective specification ) shall be attached to the extreme ends of the vertical NEWARS of the flaps by means of foot tabs which shall overlap both sides of the bottom edge. 3.6 Side Walls

PURDAHS)

3.5.1 The front and back flaps sewn to the fly shall be divided centrally. Lacing loops made from 4 mm diameter cotton line shall be sewn by hand using 2 mm diameter cotton line, or by machine using sewing thread of 590 dtex x 3 ( lOs/3 ) or 500 dtex X 4 ( 12s/4) count at the centre of the 50 mm wide vertical strengthening JVEWAR provided in the inside edge of the outer flap to correspond with the eyelets. The ends of the lacing cotton line shall be knotted and secured ~firmly under the caps at the top and under the tabs at the bottom.

3.6.1 The side walls shall Abe in continuation of the inner fly. The NEWAR in continuation of those in the fly shall run and extend to full length in the side walls. Metal dees or foot loops (as specified in the respective specification ) shall be attached to extreme ends of the vertical jVEWARS of the walls, by means of foot tabs which shall overlap both sides of the bottom edge of the walls and shall be securely sewn to it. Strips of 50 mm wide NE WAR shall be placed at the bottom edge between the folds. 3.6.2 The side walls shall be sewn to the flap or to the front and back walls ( as the case may be ) from top to bottom ( unless otherwise specified in the respective specification ). 3.7 Front and Back Walls

3.7.1 The top edge of the walls shall be attached by quilting to the inner fly. Strips of 50 mm wide NEWARS shall be placed vertically between different folds of fabric of the walls, one in the centre of width of the wall and one each equidistant from the central NEWAR. In smaller tents up to the size of 2'44 X 2'44 m ~only, the central JVEII'AR shall be provided. One 50 mm wide NEWAX shall also be placed

They shall be triangular in shape. The bottom edge shall be in line with the bottom edge of the inner Ay. For attaching the KANdT, 4 mm dia cotton lint shall be fitted to 50 mm diameter circular tabs fixed at the regular intervals of about 23 cm in the centre of the ,VEWAR situated at the bottom edge between the folds with 2 mm diameter cotton line. The position of the loops will correspond with the position of the eyelets in the KARATS. 3.7.4 The NEWARS to the cloth folds. 3.8 Detachable Wall shall be securely quilted ded at eyelets corners cotton central the top edge between folds and three shall be fixed along with it, two at the and one in the centre. 3.10 Bathroom - It shall be semi-circular or rectangular projection on the rear of the flies. It shall be made of triangular pieces of cloth strips and shall be interposed between the folds of fabrics extending from the bottom edge to the cap, at the places where the triangular pieces of the cloth shall be quilted together. Inner fold shall be interposed with NEW'ilR at corners. A NEWAR and rope shall be interposed between the folds of fabrics all round the bottom edges of the bathroom. The reinforcement at the junctions of bathroom or verandah, with the fly shall be provided with an additional XEWAR and with a double rope when specified. To minimize wastage of cloth, a maximum of three joints may be allowed in the triangular pieces. Tabs for rope shall be sewn on at the extreme ends of NEWAR leading from the cap. A pocket of 23 cm height made of same shade and fabric as that of inner field of the inner fly shall be fitted on two adjacent vertical NEWARS of the bathroom KARAT or wall. An 8 mm dia coloured rope shall be attached with 50 mm diameter circular tabs at ends. The pocket and the coloured rope shall be below the top edge of the KANAT or wall by 31 and 15'5 cm, respectively. CircuIar tabs of 50 mm diameter carrying lacing loops of 4 mm diameter cotton line shall be fitted about 23 cm apart in the centre of the bottom edge NEWAR of the bathroom for attaching the detachable K&VAT or wall. Particular care shall be exercised in making of tents to ensure that the flies and ICAJLIIS are free from puckering when the tent is pitched. 4.2 Where three folds of cloth are specified, one cross-seam may be allowed in each alternate panel of the middle fold of the walls, provided a folded seam is used as shown in Fig 2.

5. PACKING 5.1 The tents and other packed as given below. components shall be in jute

Two cross-seams may be allowed ( subject to a maximum of 10 precent of the tents ) in the roof of the flies with 2 folds, one cross-seam in the inner fold and another in the outer fold provided the seams are not in the same section and a folded seam is used. 4.3 The machine-stitching shall be carried out with cotton sewing thread of 165 dtex X 6 ( or 36~16 ) count and the average number of stitches shall be 20 to 24 per dm. 4.4 The hand-stitching shall be carried out with cotton sewing thread of 500 dtex X 4 ( or 12s/4) count.
